sources.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
sources.summary: Latent diffusion moves diffusion computation into a learned compressed representation.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

sources.title: Deepfake Nudes and Young People
sources.summary: US survey of 1,200 people aged 13–20: approximately 6% of teen respondents reported being targets of deepfake nude creation.
sources.limitations: Self-report survey subject to recall bias; sampling weighted to US demographic census standards.
sources.locator: Executive Summary & Victimization Metrics, p. 5
sources.population: Nationally representative survey of 1,200 young people aged 13–20 in the United States
sources.verified_claim: Approximately 6% of teen respondents reported being the target of a deepfake nude creation, with female teens significantly more likely to experience reputational coercion.

sources.title: The Harms of Image-Based Sexual Abuse
sources.summary: Qualitative interviews with 75 victim-survivors across the UK, Australia and New Zealand describe enduring disruption across personal and social life.
sources.limitations: Qualitative semi-structured interview methodology; emphasizes lived experiences and psychological taxonomy rather than epidemiological prevalence.
sources.locator: Empirical Section: Qualitative Interviews (pp. 31-42)
sources.population: In-depth qualitative study of 75 victim-survivors across the UK, Australia, and New Zealand
sources.verified_claim: Documents profound, enduring harms: hypervigilance, social withdrawal, loss of employment, severe trauma, and complete rupture of trust in digital spaces.

sources.title: The lived experiences and impacts of sexualized deepfake abuse
sources.summary: Qualitative interviews with 25 Australian adults, including 15 victim-survivors and 10 perpetrators, report psychological, social and occupational harms, including distress, reputational and relationship damage.
sources.limitations: Small qualitative cohort; provides crucial insights into perpetrator psychology and the false belief that synthetic media causes 'no real harm'.
sources.locator: Results: Victim-Survivor and Perpetrator Qualitative Profiles
sources.population: 25 Australian adults (15 victim-survivors and 10 self-reported perpetrators)
sources.verified_claim: Victim-survivors reported severe psychological trauma and institutional isolation; perpetrators expressed rationalizations grounded in perceived harmlessness and platform availability.

sources.title: Hilliard man sentenced for AI alteration of real minors’ images
sources.summary: Federal sentence of 14 years for two child pornography crimes; defendant admitted AI alteration of images of real children and distribution of abuse material.
sources.limitations: Adjudicated criminal conviction; proves that current federal statutes successfully apply to synthetic alterations of real children.
sources.locator: Official Press Release & Sentencing Memorandum
sources.population: Federal criminal adjudication (United States v. Defendant)
sources.verified_claim: Defendant sentenced to 14 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to producing and distributing child sexual abuse material generated by morphing faces of real local minors using AI.

sources.title: Columbus man sentenced for cyberstalking and AI-generated obscene material
sources.summary: 15-year federal sentence for multiple offenses including cyberstalking and digital forgeries
sources.limitations: Combined sentence covering multiple counts; aggregate duration reflects both interstate cyberstalking and digital forgery offenses.
sources.locator: Official Press Release & Indictment Counts
sources.population: Federal criminal prosecution for multi-victim cyberstalking and digital forgery
sources.verified_claim: Defendant sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for cyberstalking multiple victims and disseminating AI-generated sexually explicit forgeries to their employers and families.

sources.title: Crime and Policing Act 2026: explanatory notes
sources.summary: Sections 72 and 99 address child sexual abuse image-generators and purported intimate image generators; section 99 includes making, adapting and supplying, with defined defences and intermediary exemptions.
sources.limitations: Official parliamentary explanatory notes interpreting statutory text; enforcement subject to Crown court jurisprudence.
sources.locator: Division 11, Paragraphs 412-428: Generators of Purported Intimate Images
sources.population: Persons supplying, adapting, or facilitating image generation tools in the UK
sources.verified_claim: Sections 72 and 99 establish specific statutory liability for supplying software or models designed or adapted to generate CSAM or non-consensual intimate imagery, defining narrow technical exemptions.

sources.title: FTC Begins Enforcing the TAKE IT DOWN Act
sources.summary: Section 3 enforcement began 19 May 2026; covered platforms must remove qualifying intimate depictions and known identical copies within 48 hours of a valid request.
sources.limitations: Regulatory enforcement launch announcement; establishes binding administrative duties for interactive computer services.
sources.locator: Commission Policy Statement & Operational Guidelines
sources.population: Commercial websites, hosting services, and social platforms operating in the US
sources.verified_claim: FTC commenced formal nationwide enforcement of Section 3 of the Take It Down Act, establishing mandatory 48-hour takedown procedures with civil penalties up to $50,120 per violation.

sources.publisher: US National Telecommunications and Information Administration
sources.title: Dual-Use Foundation Models with Widely Available Model Weights
sources.summary: Recommended monitoring rather than immediate broad weight restrictions given then-insufficient marginal-risk evidence; preserves future targeted restriction option.
sources.limitations: US government policy report; balances open-source innovation against national security and civil protection risks.
sources.locator: Executive Summary & Policy Recommendations 1-3, pp. 6-12
sources.population: Comprehensive federal multi-stakeholder inquiry on open-weight AI models
sources.verified_claim: NTIA concluded that current evidence does not warrant immediate blanket restrictions on open model weights, recommending active monitoring while preserving the option for targeted restrictions if critical marginal risks emerge.

sources.title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: FAQ

sources.population: Citizens filing cybercrime reports across India
sources.verified_claim: Centralized statutory reporting portal with dedicated priority intake for sexually explicit content, CSAM, and digital impersonation, integrated with local state police jurisdictions and the 1930 Helpline.

sources.title: Non-Consensual Synthetic Intimate Imagery: Prevalence, Attitudes, and Knowledge in 10 Countries
sources.summary: 2.2% victimization; 1.8% perpetration, ten-country survey

sources.population: 16,145 adult survey respondents across 10 diverse countries (US, UK, India, Brazil, Japan, etc.)
sources.verified_claim: 2.2% of respondents self-reported personal victimization by non-consensual synthetic intimate imagery, while 1.8% admitted to generating or commissioning such content.

sources.title: The ecosystem of nonconsensual intimate deepfake tools online

sources.title: There Are No Limits!: AI Undressing Apps and the Normalization of Nonconsensual Intimate Deepfakes

sources.title: How common is the experience of image-based abuse among children in Australia?
sources.summary: 2,302 children completed recontact survey; 1,948 answered image-abuse questions. 3% reported a fabricated nude image made without permission at some point, 1% in past year.

sources.population: 1,948 Australian children aged 10–17 responding to the specialized image abuse module

sources.title: eSafety action prevents services nudifying Australian school children

sources.title: Submission on the Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill 2026

jurisdictions.statute: IT Act 2000, IT Rules 2021 (2026 Amendments), BNS, POCSO Act, DPDP Act
jurisdictions.timeline: 2 hours (Rule 3(2)(b) qualifying intimate-image complaints); 3 hours (Rule 3(1)(d) actual knowledge / court or government orders)
jurisdictions.scope: Distinct statutory triggers under IT Rules 2021/2026 (Rule 3(2)(b) 2h reasonable/practicable measures vs Rule 3(1)(d) 3h actual knowledge), BNS, POCSO, and DPDP Act.
obligations: Rule 3(2)(b): 2-hour window for reasonable and practicable measures on qualifying intimate-image complaints (not a universal deadline for all content).
Rule 3(1)(d): 3-hour window upon specified actual knowledge (qualifying court order or authorized government notification).
Distinguish current intermediary law from proposed upstream model-distribution regulation; not every model-hosting repository is automatically subject to every intermediary obligation.
jurisdictions.penalties: Loss of Section 79 safe harbour; BNS/POCSO criminal liability; DPDP financial penalties.
jurisdictions.gaps: No dedicated upstream statutory pre-release safety assessment mandate for open-weight model publishers.

jurisdictions.statute: TAKE IT DOWN Act (Federal) & State NCII Statutes
jurisdictions.timeline: Within 48 hours of a qualifying valid request
jurisdictions.scope: Federal covered-platform removal obligations (including known identical copies, subject to statutory requirements) enforced by the FTC, distinct from criminal provisions and state laws.
obligations: Covered platforms must remove qualifying non-consensual intimate imagery and known identical copies within 48 hours of a valid request.
Maintain accessible notice-and-removal processes subject to FTC enforcement.
Distinct from federal criminal prohibitions and state-level civil/criminal NCII statutes.
jurisdictions.penalties: FTC enforcement actions and civil penalties for covered-platform non-compliance; separate criminal penalties under applicable federal/state statutes.
jurisdictions.gaps: Does not directly regulate offline local execution of downloaded open-weight models.

jurisdictions.statute: Online Safety Act 2023 & Crime and Policing Act 2026 (ss. 99–101 in force)
jurisdictions.status: In force (OSA active; CPA 2026 ss. 99–101 commenced 29 June 2026)
jurisdictions.effectiveDate: OSA active; CPA 2026 ss. 99–101 in force 29 June 2026 (S.I. 2026/689)
jurisdictions.timeline: Expeditious takedown & Ofcom statutory enforcement notices
jurisdictions.scope: Crime and Policing Act 2026 sections 99–101 (purported intimate-image generators, taking down intimate-image content, consequential amendments) came into force on 29 June 2026 via S.I. 2026/689. Other sections vary by commencement.
obligations: Platforms in scope of the Online Safety Act must assess and mitigate illegal content risks under Ofcom codes and guidance.
Sections 99–101 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 are in force as of 29 June 2026 (S.I. 2026/689).
jurisdictions.penalties: Ofcom fines up to 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue under OSA; criminal penalties under commenced CPA 2026 ss. 99–101.
jurisdictions.gaps: Other CPA 2026 provisions depend on separate commencement orders; cross-border open-weight mirror enforcement remains challenging.

jurisdictions.statute: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, AI Act (2024/1689 Art. 50) & Digital Services Act
jurisdictions.effectiveDate: Adopted 8 July 2026; Published 24 July 2026; Applicable 2 Dec 2026
jurisdictions.timeline: Expeditious notice-and-action under DSA; AI prohibitions from 2 Dec 2026
jurisdictions.scope: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Art. 1(7), printed p. 18) addresses specified AI systems generating/manipulating non-consensual intimate material and CSAM. As of 25 Nov 2026 cutoff, enacted but not yet applicable. Not a universal ban on open-weight AI models.
obligations: Prohibitions on specified abusive AI systems take effect 2 December 2026, subject to defined conditions, safeguards, and exceptions.
AI Act Art. 50 transparency and machine-readable marking duties (applicable 2 August 2026).
DSA systemic risk mitigation duties for Very Large Online Platforms.
jurisdictions.penalties: Administrative fines under AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and DSA enforcement frameworks.
jurisdictions.gaps: Watermarking/provenance signals can be stripped; prohibitions are not yet applicable as of 25 Nov 2026 cutoff.

jurisdictions.statute: Online Safety Act 2021, Industry Codes/Standards & eSafety Enforcement
jurisdictions.timeline: 24 hours from formal eSafety removal notice
jurisdictions.scope: Image-based abuse scheme covering digitally altered or synthetic intimate depictions, plus eSafety notices to platforms and model-hosting repositories.
obligations: Comply with formal eSafety removal notices within 24 hours.
Adhere to registered Online Safety industry codes and standards.
Documented regulator outcomes: 8 services withdrew Australian access or introduced compliance measures; Hugging Face updated misuse rules following eSafety engagement.
jurisdictions.penalties: Federal Court civil penalties (e.g., AUD 343,500 civil penalty order in 2025 case); service blocking directions.
jurisdictions.gaps: Service access restrictions do not establish measured population-level reductions in victimization.

jurisdictions.effectiveDate: Royal Assent 18 June 2026; commencement details pending verification
jurisdictions.scope: Addresses non-consensual sexual deepfakes; exact commencement dates and operative statutory provisions require verification against authoritative Canadian legal records before making enforceability claims.
obligations: Statutory amendments addressing non-consensual synthetic sexual depictions (subject to confirmed commencement).
Intermediary court-order compliance under applicable criminal procedure.
jurisdictions.penalties: Criminal penalties as prescribed upon commencement.
jurisdictions.gaps: Commencement status and full operative text require local primary verification.

jurisdictions.statute: Penal Code (Defamation Art. 230, Insult Art. 231) & Provider Liability Act
jurisdictions.timeline: Notice-and-takedown under Provider Liability Limitation Act
jurisdictions.scope: Previously established findings note possible criminal defamation or insult depending on case facts, alongside civil privacy/portrait rights.
obligations: Voluntary platform moderation upon valid infringement notice.
Sender identification disclosure upon court order.
jurisdictions.penalties: Criminal defamation/insult penalties where statutory elements are met; civil tort liability.
jurisdictions.gaps: No standalone deepfake-specific statutory offence established in retained baseline.

jurisdictions.statute: Act on Special Cases Concerning Punishment of Sexual Crimes (Art. 14-2)
jurisdictions.scope: English statutory text addresses non-consensual editing or synthesis of a person's face, body, or voice into sexual depictions.
obligations: Prohibits non-consensual sexual synthesis and distribution.
Telecommunications operators must execute blocking/filtering orders.
jurisdictions.penalties: Statutory criminal imprisonment and fines under Art. 14-2.
jurisdictions.gaps: Cross-border enforcement against offshore encrypted channels remains difficult.

corrections.title: India Helpline 1930 Scope & Regional Number Withholding

corrections.reason: Prevents misrouting survivors in crisis to a financial fraud hotline.
